text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures pared gains in late trading but were expected to broadly trade in a range over the next sessions, lacking the momentum to extend gains amassed late last week. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 98.01, up 0.05 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended unchanged from Friday's levels, giving up early gains in line with the weaker undertone in Bunds and Treasuries. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-30/32, up 1/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures and PIBOR contracts built on last week's strong gains, surprising many participants who had forecast some consolidation on Monday. Traders said positioning ahead of the expiry of the September bond future today was the initial driving force and calm returned to the market in the afternoon. German economic releases later in the week were now the main focus. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 123.84, up 0.22 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets lived up to their reputation for quicksilver moves, streaking ahead of the pack and forging a new contract high in December LIFFE futures. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 117.79, up 0.39 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Prices of U.S. Treasury securities were little changed and trading in extremely tight ranges near midday after ignoring the only economic report scheduled for release on Monday -- July business inventories. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-24/32, up 1/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.96 percent.
JAPAN - Japanese markets were closed today for a public holiday. They will reopen tomorrow. In after hours trading on Friday the September future on LIFFE was trading at 121.51.

EUROBONDS - Eurobonds sprang to life, with new issues in a variety of currencies. Two emerging market countries came to the fore. South Africa priced its 500 million mark seven-year bond to yield 140 basis points over Bunds. Mexico set a $750 million 20-year bond to be priced 450-462.5 b.p. over U.S. Treasuries. Also in dollars, Nordbanken set a $125 million perpetual FRN. ING added 50 million marks to its Morocco-linked bond. Siam City Bank is expected to launch a $100 million five-year bond on Tuesday.
